summary.text: Pentheus king of Thebes denied the god born to his aunt Semele; Dionysus drove the women to Cithaeron in frenzy, and Agave the king's mother tore her son apart with her bare hands, thinking him a lion.

chapters.title: Semele's fire
chapters.text: Semele, daughter of Cadmus, lay with Zeus and asked to see him in his true form; the lightning consumed her, but Hermes snatched the infant Dionysus from her womb and stitched him into Zeus' thigh until the god was born again — the twice-born, whom Hera's jealousy would hound all his days.

chapters.title: The stranger at the gates
chapters.text: When Dionysus came back to Thebes as a god, Pentheus son of Echion and Agave forbade his rites and imprisoned the maenads. The stranger — the god in disguise — escaped his bonds and promised to show the king the sacred women on Mount Cithaeron if Pentheus would dress as one of them.

chapters.title: The maenads' prey
chapters.text: On the mountain the Theban women, maddened by Dionysus, tore Pentheus limb from limb. Agave his mother bore his head on a thyrsus, thinking it the head of a lion, and only when the frenzy passed did she see what she had done to her son.
